liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Crazy Fingers** (2 reviews): Crazy Fingers is sweet, with full bass sound; Reviewer hears some playing flaws, citing a poor Crazy Fingers jam [16][18]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): He's Gone was dedicated to Boston Celtics player Len Bias, who had died days earlier of a drug overdose; The He's Gone into Smokestack Lightning is slinky and sounds distinctive for 1986 [13][16]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums, with intricate rhythms and Mickey's beam, drew the reviewer deeply into drum segments [16]
- **Space** (1 review): The electronic drum space anticipates club chill-out music by over fifteen years [18]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): Reviewer loves the Comes A Time [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **encore1 I Need A Miracle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **encore2 U.S. Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-05-11.156611.nakomni.holbrook.flac24** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 145 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: The entire first track had a bad right channel, so the left was patched into mono; a loud PA crackle occurs midway [1]
- **gd1986-05-11.140257.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: source not stated; 22 songs; 148 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1986-05-11.168552.RealisticStereoCardioidCondenser33919.ont.flac1644**: source not stated; 21 songs; 141 min [6]
- **gd86-05-11.sbd.hinko.26557.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the recording quality of this soundboard, which captures the Frost's freakish atmosphere [18]
- **gd1986-05-11.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81626.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 3.44/5 by 9 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer notes second-set setlist numbers do not match the actual tracks in this archive [23]

## Around the show

- Crowd chanted for Phil before the opener, then for Brent, which led to Good Times, and also for Steve Parish [15]
- Audience coaxed the band back for a second encore, which was U.S. Blues [15]
- Reviewer says Jerry seemed only half present, with Bobby's guitar filling parts expected from Jerry, and the band picked up the slack [23]
- It was the taper's fourth Dead show, a few days before their 21st birthday, after a failed attempt at the May 3 Cal Expo show [6]
- Reviewer finds this soundboard pretty good but not quite as strong as the band's earlier years [14]
- The He's Gone dedicated to Len Bias was actually played at the Greek a month later, not at this show [15]
- Reviewer says this archive has the best sound among the copies of this show [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-05-11.156611.nakomni.holbrook.flac24**: taped by Executive Crew, Mike Davis, Kenny Davis, John Hance, Aaron; patched out of Poris/Olness rig; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: 1GEN AUDCA speed corrected 2.25% usig Audacity Microphones: Jaime Poris custom mics: Nakamichi capsules customized, attached to plexiglass plates spread 20… [1]. Also: The tapers had been told not to go front-of-board at the Frost, so they patched into Aaron's crew's custom mic, preamp and dbx system [1]
- **gd1986-05-11.140257.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Charlie Miller, Jim Wise, Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 (120 degree ORTF)> Oade M118 > Sony PCM-F1; Transfer Info: Master Oade PCM (unknown deck/hardware/software) > hard disk >… [2]
- **gd1986-05-11.168552.RealisticStereoCardioidCondenser33919.ont.flac1644**: taped by OldNeumanntapr; transferred by OldNeumanntapr; source: OTS; Left, Realistic Stereo Cardioid Condenser 33-919 (On Stand) >Sharp Boom Box [6]. Also: Taper used a borrowed Realistic stereo microphone and stand from Cuesta College's music department, recording to a boom box [6]
- **gd86-05-11.sbd.hinko.26557.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Darryl Hinko; source: flac16 SBD > MC > C > DAT > CD > EAC > FLAC [7]
- **gd1986-05-11.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.81626.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell MX-90) D [8]. Also: Beyer M88 to cassette master, then Sound Forge to CD, by Charlie Connor; cassettes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [8]
